job.title: Document Controller
job.description:
The Company
﻿Our client is a global leader in construction and part of a renowned Construction Group. With a diverse portfolio spanning various sectors, they boast a history of delivering complex and impactful projects worldwide. Their commitment to innovation and sustainability is evident in their current undertaking in Australia, a significant wastewater treatment plant upgrade in Canberra. This collaborative venture with their subsidiary, is valued at $385 million and encompasses a 10-year program.

The Role
﻿Reporting to the Program Manager, The Document Controller will be responsible for establishing and operating document control and records management processes and products in accordance with relevant standards, policies and procedures. You will ensure that the project complies with quality document control, records management procedures and meet compliance requirements.

Responsibilities

  • Organising, managing, and maintaining company documents, ensuring accuracy, quality, and integrity
  • Facilitating easy retrieval of documents by employees, ensuring that essential documents are readily available for project planning.
  • Conduct regular checks to verify the accuracy and completeness of documents and taking corrective actions when required
  • Working closely with cross-functional teams to facilitate document-related communication and ensure seamless collaboration across all departments.
  • Ensuring that all documents adhere to relevant regulatory standards and internal policies
  • Identifying and implementing document management process improvements
  • Co-administer company EDMS tool
  • Provide training and guidance to employees and key internal/external stakeholders on document control processes and best practices


Requirements

  • 5 to 10 years' experience in document control or related capacity.
  • Explosure to large, greenfield infrastructure projects highly regarded.
  • Strong Proficiency in Aconex, InEight & MS Suite required.
  • Strong organisational skills and high attention to detail
  • Excellent communication skills

job.title: Senior Consultant / Manager
job.description:
The company
﻿Our client is a global management consulting firm specializing in strategy and operations across technology-intensive industries. With a presence in multiple countries, including Australia, they deliver impactful business transformations, operational excellence, and strategic initiatives tailored to the unique challenges of industries such as aerospace, transportation, energy, and infrastructure.

In Australia, they are actively supporting clients in navigating complex business environments, leveraging their expertise to drive sustainable and lasting results.


The Role
Reporting to the Senior Leadership Team, the Senior Consultant/Manager will be responsible for leading high-impact projects, driving operational improvements, and delivering actionable insights for clients across various industries. 


Responsibilities

  • Lead and execute complex analyses, structuring insights and delivering tailored solutions for clients.
  • Develop and present actionable recommendations to senior management, guiding transformational change initiatives.
  • Foster and maintain trust-based relationships with clients, managing improvement initiatives and building long-term partnerships.
  • Mentor and support junior consultants, accelerating their professional growth and development.
  • Collaborate on business development activities, including proposal preparation and market analysis.
  • Contribute to internal operations, including marketing, recruitment, and training initiatives.


About You
You are a strategic thinker with extensive experience in management consulting, particularly in industries such as aerospace, transportation, or energy. You thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments and bring a proven track record in delivering innovative solutions and managing complex projects.

  • A degree in Engineering or Business (post-graduate qualifications preferred).
  • At least 4 years of management consulting experience, with a focus on technology-intensive industries.
  • Demonstrated leadership in managing teams and overseeing large-scale projects.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Motivated, energetic, and eager to grow in an entrepreneurial and supportive environment.
  • Fluent in English and willing to travel within Australia as required.
  • Australian citizenship is mandatory.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience in technology-driven industries such as defence, energy, or utilities.
  • Expertise in fostering cross-cultural collaborations in a global context.

Benefits

  • 40% Bonus

job.title: Senior Design Engineer
job.description:
Shape the ground beneath Australia's biggest infrastructure projects. This role suits a technically sharp Senior Design Engineer who thrives on geotechnical challenges, loves variety, and wants to see their designs come to life on site.


The Company

Our client is a global leader in ground improvement and foundation engineering, delivering design-and-construct solutions across Australia and New Zealand. Part of a world-renowned civil engineering group, they combine local delivery with cutting-edge expertise in soil reinforcement, foundation systems, and geotechnical innovation. Their projects span ports, rail corridors, industrial facilities, and large-scale public infrastructure earning a reputation for technical excellence, innovation, and on-time delivery.

The Role

As Senior Design Engineer, youll lead the technical design of ground improvement and foundation solutions from feasibility through detailed design and construction support. Working closely with project and construction teams, youll ensure each design is safe, efficient, and buildable.
You will take ownership of modelling, design documentation, and client liaison while mentoring junior engineers and contributing to value engineering for tenders and live projects.

Responsibilities

  • Deliver design packages for ground improvement and foundation systems (e.g. rigid inclusions, stone columns, vacuum consolidation, dynamic compaction)
  • Perform advanced geotechnical analyses, modelling, and reporting to support D&C projects.
  • Liaise with internal teams and external stakeholders to optimise constructability and cost efficiency. 
  • Review and verify calculations, drawings, and documentation for accuracy and compliance.
  • Provide design support during construction, addressing technical queries and design changes.
  • Contribute to tenders and proposals through design input and technical presentations.
  • Mentor and guide junior engineers, fostering quality, safety, and collaboration within the team.


    Requirements

    • Bachelors degree in Civil |Geotechnical Engineering highly regarded
    • Min. 5+ years' experience in geotechnical or foundation design for large infrastructure projects.
    • Strong technical proficiency in analysis and modelling tools such as PLAXIS or similar.
    • Experience with D&C delivery and interface between design and construction.
    • Excellent communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.
    • Passion for innovation and practical, buildable design outcomes.


      If you're ready to take the next step in your career, apply now or contact ilan@rec-partners.com.au for more details.
      Follow our Rec-Partners LinkedIn page to stay updated on our latest opportunities.

job.title: BIM Coordinator
job.description:
About the Company
The company is a well-established infrastructure contractor delivering large-scale civil and engineering projects across Australia. With a strong pipeline of government-backed works and long-term programs, they operate in complex, multi-disciplinary environments where digital engineering and BIM are central to delivery. Known for their structured systems, collaborative project culture, and focus on innovation, they continue to invest in technology-driven construction methods to improve efficiency, coordination, and project outcomes.


The Role
﻿Reporting to the Engineering Manager, ﻿you will sit at the centre of project delivery, acting as the bridge between design, engineering, and construction teams. Working across both pre-construction and delivery phases, you will coordinate BIM workflows, manage and integrate models from multiple stakeholders, and drive clash-free outcomes. This is a hands-on role combining coordination, modelling, and stakeholder engagement, where your ability to bring structure, clarity, and technical insight will directly influence project performance.


Key Responsibilities & Deliverables

  • Prepare and support BIM workflows across design and construction phases
  • Coordinate and aggregate BIM models from consultants and subcontractors
  • Perform clash detection and produce detailed coordination reports
  • Maintain BIM models, object libraries, and CAD standards
  • Support construction planning through 4D simulations and quantity take-offs
  • Ensure adherence to BIM execution plans and project standards
  • Collaborate closely with engineering and site teams to resolve design conflicts
  • Provide BIM support for scheduling, costing, and project coordination
  • Assist in value engineering and buildability improvements
  • Deliver BIM training and support to project stakeholders

﻿

What We Are Looking For﻿

  • ﻿Relevant tertiary qualification in Engineering or similar
  • Min 3+ years' experience in BIM coordination within construction/infrastructure
  • Strong proficiency in Autodesk Revit and Navisworks (essential)
  • Solid understanding of construction methodologies and project lifecycles
  • Experience working across multiple stakeholders and disciplines
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and coordination skills
  • Ability to manage deadlines and operate in fast-paced project environments
  • Clear communication and strong attention to detail

What's on Offer﻿

  • ﻿Long-term infrastructure program offering stability and continuity
  • Exposure to complex, multi-disciplinary projects
  • Strong pipeline of government-backed works
  • Opportunity to develop into senior digital engineering roles
  • Collaborative and technically driven project environment
  • Competitive salary aligned with experience﻿

job.title: Contracts Administrator
job.description:
About the Company

This global construction and infrastructure leader is delivering some of Australia's most complex and critical water, energy, and transport projects. With a strong national presence and major project wins across ANZ, they are continuing to grow their footprint through landmark joint ventures and long-term partnerships.

The company is backed by one of the largest global construction conglomerate and operates with a collaborative delivery model underpinned by world-class engineering and safety standards.


The Role

Based in Canberra and reporting to the Commercial Manager, you will take ownership of subcontract and procurement administration across the full project lifecycle — from tender evaluations and package letting through to subcontract administration, variations, claims management and cost reporting during construction. You will work closely with operations, procurement and JV stakeholders to ensure financial commitments align with approved budgets, contractual positions are protected, and supply chain performance delivers optimal commercial outcomes.

Key Responsibilities & Deliverables

Tender Stage:

  • Facilitate tender evaluations and prepare evaluation reports for low-risk contracts
  • Review subcontractor and supplier pricing, prepare comparison sheets and recommendations
  • Support drafting of subcontracts, purchase orders and consultancy agreements
  • Negotiate competitive pricing and commercial terms
  • Prepare schedules of quantities, cost breakdowns and procurement timeframes
  • Contribute to green costing, lifecycle costing and carbon considerations in procurement decisions

Construction Stage:

  • Administer subcontractor and supplier appointments
  • Maintain variation, delay and claims registers and support formal claim preparation
  • Monitor progress against budget and report on commercial performance
  • Prepare contractual correspondence and notices to protect the company's position
  • Coordinate procurement logistics and maintain up-to-date supplier registers
  • Work closely with site teams to manage day-to-day commercial activities


What We Are Looking For

  • Min. 3+ years' experience in contract administration, commercial or procurement roles within construction/infrastructure
  • Relevant tertiary qualification in construction management, engineering, quantity surveying or similar
  • Strong understanding of subcontract management and commercial processes
  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously and meet demanding deadlines
  • Highly organised with strong analytical and negotiation skills
  • Comfortable engaging with clients, JV partners and internal stakeholders
  • Proficient in document management systems such as SharePoint
  • Resilient, detail-oriented and confident operating in a fast-paced project environment

What's on Offer

  • AUD130,000 – 140,000 + Super, depending on experience
  • Flexible working model with a balanced mix of office, site and WFH
  • Long-term project stability on a nationally significant public infrastructure program
  • Clear pathways to progress into Senior CA or Commercial roles
  • Exposure to complex contract structures within a disciplined JV environment
  • A collaborative, high-performance culture where accountability and autonomy are valued

job.title: Rail Safety Manager
job.description:
About the Company
Our client is a major transportation company, playing a critical role in keeping a large urban population moving every day. They are responsible for both operations and maintenance of a complex fleet and asset base, within a highly regulated and safety-critical environment. With ongoing investment in reliability, asset performance, and system improvements, they offer a stable platform for senior professionals looking to influence safety, quality, and operational outcomes at scale.


The Role
Reporting to the Head of Maintenance Strategy, this role will lead the Safety and Quality function, driving the implementation, performance, and continuous improvement of both the Safety Management System and Quality Management System.
This is a pivotal role in shaping safety culture, ensuring regulatory compliance, and embedding quality standards across engineering and maintenance activities, while influencing senior stakeholders and operational leaders.


Key Responsibilities & Deliverables.

  • Lead and continuously improve the SMS to ensure compliance with relevant OH&S legislation
  • Drive safety assurance activities including audits, inspections, investigations, and corrective actions
  • Champion safety culture initiatives including Just & Fair reporting, leading indicators, and life-saving rules
  • Establish and manage a Quality Management System aligned with ISO 9001 principles
  • Oversee non-conformance and CAPA processes, ensuring root-cause analysis and effective resolution
  • Monitor and report on safety and quality metrics, driving continuous improvement initiatives
  • Partner with senior stakeholders, regulators, and operational teams to ensure compliance and performance


What We Are Looking For

  • Extensive experience in safety, quality, or engineering leadership roles within rail or complex infrastructure environments
  • Strong knowledge of SMS and Quality frameworks in regulated industries
  • Proven experience leading safety programs, audits, investigations, and cultural transformation initiatives
  • Deep understanding of rail safety legislation highly regarded
  • Demonstrated leadership capability, with experience managing teams and influencing senior stakeholders
  • Strong analytical mindset with the ability to interpret data and drive actionable insights
  • Confident communicator, capable of engaging across executive, operational, and regulatory audiences
  • Tertiary qualification in engineering, safety, quality, or related discipline (or equivalent experience)


What's on Offer

  • AUD170,000 – 180,000 + Super (negotiable based on experience)
  • Senior leadership position with real influence on safety and operational outcomes
  • Exposure to a large-scale, complex urban transport environment
  • Strong organisational backing with long-term stability and investment
  • Flexible working arrangements with a mix of office and operational engagement
